recent_posts.title: Why I Built Vykar Backup: A Faster, Simpler Rust Backup Tool
recent_posts.summary: Vykar is a new open-source Rust-based backup tool that consolidates configuration, scheduling, backup, restore, and monitoring into a single binary with one YAML config file. Built by the creator of BorgBase and Vorta, it addresses fragmentation in the backup ecosystem where tools like Borg, Restic, and Kopia each require additional wrappers. Key features include built-in scheduling via a daemon, a desktop GUI, WebDAV snapshot browsing, support for local/S3/SFTP/REST backends, and native command dumps for streaming Docker database backups (Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB) without temp files or bash scripts. Benchmarks show it outperforms Borg, Restic, Rustic, and Kopia on backup and restore speed with lower CPU usage. It's early-stage but open source on GitHub.

recent_posts.title: Scanopy: Self-Hosted Network Scanner That Builds a Live Topology Map
recent_posts.summary: Scanopy is an open-source, self-hosted network discovery tool built for homelabs. It runs a server and one or more daemons (dockerized) that scan VLANs via ARP and full 65k-port scans, detect 200+ common self-hosted services through pattern matching, poll network devices via SNMP v2c (including LLDP/CDP neighbor data), and generate an interactive, self-updating topology map. Features include versioned and branchable topologies, editable visualizations, CSV export, a granular API with scoped keys, and a UI for manually assigning unidentified ports. Licensed under AGPL-3.0.

recent_posts.title: OpenDroneLog: A Self Hosted DJI Flight Log Dashboard
recent_posts.summary: OpenDroneLog is an open-source, self-hosted flight log dashboard for DJI drones and Litchi CSV exports. It stores all data locally in a DuckDB database and offers interactive flight maps with replay, telemetry charts, battery health tracking, smart deduplication, and export to CSV/JSON/GPX/KML. Deployable via Docker Compose with optional automatic log ingestion from a mounted folder using cron-based sync. Built with a Rust/Axum backend, Nginx, and React frontend. Licensed under AGPL-3.0.

recent_posts.title: HarborFM - Self-Hosted Podcast Creator
recent_posts.summary: HarborFM is a free, open-source, self-hosted podcast creation platform inspired by the now-defunct Anchor.FM. It lets users build episodes from reusable audio segments (recordings, uploads, intros, outros), trim and arrange them, and generate a final audio or video file. Key features include a segment-based episode editor with non-destructive trimming, WebRTC group call recording, Whisper-based transcription with AI summaries, Podcast 2.0 chapter markers, per-show RSS feeds, private tokenized subscriber feeds, analytics, live multi-user collaboration, and flexible deployment destinations (S3/R2, FTP, SFTP, WebDAV, IPFS, SMB). Deployment is supported via Docker, Docker Compose, or Terraform scripts targeting AWS or Vultr. Admin controls cover SSO (OIDC/SAML), 2FA, custom domains with automatic SSL, and configurable LLM/transcription services (Ollama or OpenAI).

recent_posts.title: Eonvelope – Self Hosted Email Archiving Made Simple
recent_posts.summary: Eonvelope is an open-source, self-hosted email archiving solution that supports IMAP, POP3, Exchange, and JMAP protocols. It offers flexible archiving with configurable background tasks, threaded conversation browsing, and spam filtering. The tool integrates with popular self-hosted services like Paperless-ngx, Immich, Nextcloud, SearXNG, and Grafana. Setup takes about 5 minutes via Docker or Kubernetes, includes SSL by default, and features a slim mode for low-resource devices. Built with Python and HTML, it has 98% test coverage and provides a full REST API with Prometheus metrics endpoint.

recent_posts.title: Two Years with HostHatch AMD Cloud VPS
recent_posts.summary: A long-term user shares their experience running a lightweight application on HostHatch's AMD Cloud VPS in Chicago. The setup includes 1 CPU core, 2GB RAM, 11GB NVMe storage, and 1TB bandwidth running Debian 12. Performance has been consistent with fast disk operations, predictable network latency, and reliable uptime. Support responses have been quick and helpful. The author values the straightforward interface without upselling and notes HostHatch sponsors their site, though this review is unpaid.

recent_posts.title: Building a self hosted voice AI mirror with Raspberry Pi and Ollama
recent_posts.summary: MirrorMate is a self-hosted voice-first AI assistant that runs behind a half mirror, combining hardware (Raspberry Pi, display, microphone) with software (Next.js, SQLite). It supports two deployment modes: minimal cloud setup using OpenAI APIs, or fully local using Ollama, VOICEVOX, and faster-whisper. The system features RAG-based memory for personal context, YAML-driven configuration for swapping LLM/TTS/STT providers, a plugin system for extensibility, and built-in integrations for weather, calendar, and reminders. The architecture keeps the Pi thin (UI and audio only) while offloading heavy AI workloads to a separate inference server, connected via Tailscale for privacy.

recent_posts.title: Portabase: A Lightweight Self-Hosted Database Backup Solution
recent_posts.summary: Portabase is a self-hosted database backup and restore tool supporting PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB. It uses a central server for management and lightweight agents that operate in outbound pull mode, eliminating the need to expose databases to the internet. The platform features three retention strategies (fixed count, time-based, GFS rotation), supports S3-compatible storage backends, and integrates with notification platforms like Slack and Discord. The central server is built with Next.js 16 and PostgreSQL, while agents have been refactored from Python to Rust for better performance and a 4x smaller Docker image.

recent_posts.title: Jotty·Page - Self-Hosted Notes and Checklists
recent_posts.summary: Jotty is a self-hosted note-taking and checklist application designed for quick access and local file storage. It features a WYSIWYG/markdown editor, checklist-to-Kanban conversion, OIDC authentication, PGP and xChaCha encryption options, PWA support, full REST API, and community-maintained translations in six languages. The tool stores files locally, offers powerful search, and allows extensive customization including custom themes and CSS styling.

recent_posts.title: Why developers should try self-hosting at least once
recent_posts.summary: Self-hosting teaches developers practical skills that cloud platforms abstract away. By running your own services, you learn how software actually operates in production, understand networking fundamentals like DNS and reverse proxies, develop security awareness, and naturally pick up DevOps skills. The experience builds troubleshooting confidence and can shape career paths toward infrastructure and cloud engineering roles. Starting is accessible with beginner-friendly tools like Ghost for blogging, Pangolin for reverse proxying, Beszel for monitoring, and Dockhand for Docker management.
